text:
- chief complaint: the patient presents with right knee pain for one week after a slip and fall while working on their property, with a pop felt at the time of injury.
- history of present illness: the patient fell while doing yard work and felt a pop in the right knee. Pain is worse with flexion, extension, and movement under pressure, and the knee is mildly swollen. Pain is about 4/10 with mobility and minimal at rest. The patient has been taking ibuprofen for swelling. An x-ray showed no fracture or bony abnormality.
- physical examination: tenderness over the medial aspect of the right knee, pain with flexion and extension, mild edema and effusion. No lateral tenderness. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart shows a known grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Blood pressure at the visit was 150/70.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right knee pain, swelling, and a popping sensation at injury. The patient denies chest pain, abdominal pain, and shortness of breath.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: ibuprofen 800 mg by mouth twice daily. Lisinopril 20 mg continued unchanged.
- follow-up instructions: knee brace, ice the knee for 20 minutes at a time 3 to 4 times daily, elevate the leg and avoid weight-bearing for a couple of weeks, referral to nutrition for sodium reduction (goal about 2300 mg/day), and return for a follow-up visit.
